candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — antepartum health promotion and exercise counseling
candidate.educational_objective: Counsel a healthy client with an uncomplicated pregnancy to obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity weekly, with gradual progression and individualized adjustment when needed.

options.A: Avoid starting aerobic exercise during pregnancy if you were previously sedentary; wait until after delivery to begin a regular program.
options.B: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week when there are no obstetric or medical contraindications; if new to exercise, start slowly and increase gradually.
options.C: Replace moderate-intensity activity with vigorous-intensity exercise during pregnancy even if you were not exercising vigorously before pregnancy.
options.D: Continue the same exercise plan throughout pregnancy without modification because normal physiologic changes do not require adjustment.

candidate.rationale: ACOG states that, in the absence of obstetric or medical complications or contraindications, physical activity during pregnancy is safe and desirable. Pregnant clients should ideally obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week. Clients who are new to exercise should start slowly and gradually increase activity, while some modification may be needed as pregnancy progresses. Therefore B is correct. A incorrectly delays safe activity until postpartum, C recommends vigorous exercise without regard to prior activity level, and D incorrectly excludes modification despite normal pregnancy-related changes.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In uncomplicated pregnancy without contraindications, exercise is safe and desirable; obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity weekly, and if new to exercise start slowly and increase gradually; exercise may need modification during pregnancy.
